questions.stem_markdown: The lengths of pencils made at a factory are normally distributed. The standard deviation of the lengths is $\sigma$ cm, and the mean is supposed to be 10 cm. He then carries out a hypothesis test.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: For standardising. Must have square root 50.
Accept if seen in part (i) but not in (ii). Accept population mean but not just mean.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: [Reject H_{0} ] There is sufficient evidence [at 2.5% level] to suggest that mean length is greater than 10 cm. Or There is suff evidence to support the inspectors thought /claim.
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: No contradictions. In context. Not definite. Accept ‘... that mean length has increased’ Note 2 tail test scores **B0M1A0**.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: No, because population distribution [of lengths] is normal

questions.stem_markdown:

Later, Emma has to choose two people at random from three people.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: e.g. $$P(n=0)=\frac{1}{4}$$ and $$P(n=1)=\frac{1}{2}$$ or $$P(n=1)=2 \times P(n=0)$$ or similar
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Numerical justification or there is one way to get 0 but two ways to get 1, or similar **B1B1**.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: Choose $PQ$ or $QR$ or $RP$ soi or reject $R$ or $P$ or $Q$ soi

OE. Using the score on the dice to give each of the three cases equal probability. More than one throw of the dice scores **B0B0**.

questions.stem_markdown:
A random variable $X$ has probability density function given by

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} ax & 0 \leqslant x \leqslant b, \\ 0 & \text{otherwise}, \end{cases}$$

where $a$ and $b$ are constants.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Attempt triangle area or integrate $$f(x)$$ (ignore limits) and $$= 1$$.
Attempt to integrate $$x f(x)$$. Ignore limits.
OE. Integrate $$f(x)$$ with limits 0 and their E(X) Condone $$a$$ instead of $$\frac{2}{b^2}$$ Or using areas, $$\text{prob} = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2b}{3} \times \frac{2}{3}ab$$
Correct integration and limits, **FT** their $$E(X)$$. Need $$\frac{2}{b^2}$$. Or $$\text{prob} = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2b}{3} \times \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{2b}{b^2}$$.
Must see correct expression after substituting limits. Convincingly obtained. No errors seen. Or expression correctly simplified.

questions.stem_markdown:
In the past, one quarter of job applicants at a certain firm had first-class degrees. A change is made in the job description and a director of the firm believes that, on average, the proportion of job applicants with first class degrees has decreased.

In the month following the change, there were 35 job applicants, and $r$ of these had first-class degrees. The firm carried out a hypothesis test at the 4% significance level to test the director's belief.

In another month, the director carries out a similar test at the 4% significance level using the 35 job applicants from that month.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Dep on above two correct probabilities seen and at least one comparison with 0.04.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: Concluding proportion has decreased when in fact it hasn't
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Or concluding that the director's belief is correct when in fact it isn't.
Attempt 1 – P($r \leq 3$) with B(35, 0.05). Expressions or terms.
